production_robots_baseline.effect: All automatic agents that honor wildcard robots rules are currently allowed unless a more specific live rule exists.
production_robots_baseline.live_edge_result: PASS for tested official crawler UA claims. Cloudflare returns 200 for curl default and all tested Google/Bing/OpenAI/Anthropic/Perplexity crawler UAs on /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /screener/companies/. Cloudflare returns 403 for Python-urllib-style UA on the same paths; actual urllib succeeds when given curl UA, isolating the behavior to User-Agent policy rather than Python/TLS client fingerprint.

principles: Search/retrieval access and model-training access are separate policy decisions.
User-agent strings are claimed identity only and are not trusted bot identity by themselves.
Private/noindex behavior remains enforced by application access control and page-level directives, not robots.txt alone.
Crawler access must not change application content or create crawler-specific pages.
WAF allow rules for bots must use provider verification evidence where available, not User-Agent strings alone.

findings: curl default User-Agent returned HTTP 200 on all three paths.
curl using Python-urllib/3.10 User-Agent returned HTTP 403 on all three paths.
actual Python urllib default returned HTTP 403 on all three paths.
actual Python urllib using curl/7.81.0 User-Agent returned HTTP 200 on all three paths.
All tested official crawler User-Agent claims returned HTTP 200 on all three paths.
No tested crawler request required redirects, cookies, or a visible challenge page.
edge_observation.classification: Cloudflare User-Agent-based denial of Python-urllib-style clients; not a Python/TLS-stack fingerprint block and not a block of the tested search/AI crawler UA families.
edge_observation.security_note: UA-only probes establish accessibility of claimed agent strings, not verified crawler identity.

cross_product_access_sample.methodology: One representative URL selected from each of the 10 live child sitemaps; tested with Googlebot, bingbot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot User-Agent claims.
cross_product_access_sample.conclusion: PASS: sampled public acquisition pages across every live sitemap family are accessible through Cloudflare to all five tested search/retrieval crawler UA families without redirect, cookie, or visible challenge requirements.
cross_product_access_sample.caveat: UA probing demonstrates accessibility of claimed crawler strings, not verified crawler identity.

observability_preflight.conclusion: SG-01E/F require a Caddy observability change. Current logs are runtime/admin logs only; there is no HTTP access-log stream and no trusted-proxy real-client-IP parsing.
observability_preflight.security_constraint: Do not trust CF-Connecting-IP unless the direct peer is validated as Cloudflare via Caddy trusted_proxies or equivalent origin-network restriction.

observability_design.approach: Caddy native JSON access log on marketdeck.in only, plus explicit cf_connecting_ip and cf_ray fields via log_append.
observability_design.real_ip_strategy: Do not change Caddy trusted_proxies/request semantics in the first observability release. Preserve request behavior and verify that request.remote_ip is within current official Cloudflare CIDRs before treating the separately logged CF-Connecting-IP value as the visitor/source IP.
observability_design.maximum_uncompressed_nominal_window: approximately 120MiB including active file plus five 20MiB rolled files; rolled files are compressed by default
observability_design.rationale: Central observability with bounded disk use and no application changes or proxy-header behavior changes.
